newsitem.title: USA: Puerto Rico Gov, CEOs lobby Congress on wage credit.
newsitem.headline: Puerto Rico Gov, CEOs lobby Congress on wage credit.

text.p: Puerto Rico Governor Pedro Rossello and top U.S. corporate executives on Tuesday called on the Congress to extend indefinitely key wage credits under the Internal Revenue Code for U.S. companies doing business in the commonwealth.

"This resolution signed today by this delegation of important corporate leaders represents a step ... toward the creation of a sustainable economic development platform for Puerto Rico," Rossello said at a press briefing here.

Joining Rossello were top executives from 25 firms, among them these chief executive officers: Charles Heimbold of Bristol Meyers & Squibb; Melvin Goodes of Warner Lambert; William Sheperd of Allergan, Inc; Vernon Loucks of Baxter International; and Jackson Ratcliffe of Hubbell Incorporated.
Rossello and CEOs particularly want Congress to extend indefinitely a wage credit for Puerto Rico under Section 30-A of the Internal Revenue Code that expires in 10 years.

"As a U.S. based company with substantial manufacturing operations in the Commonwealth, Allergan strongly supports the continuation of the wage credit beyond the 10-year sunset and well into the future," Allergan CEO William Shepherd said at the press briefing.
Rossello said Tuesday's resolution aims to "protect and preserve all current federal economic incentives and benefits available to U.S. companies doing business in Puerto Rico."
